constraints: The netlist must be a flat, single-clock gate-level design using only cells declared in cell_library.v (DFF_POSEDGE, DFF_NEGEDGE, and standard combinational gates AND2, OR2, NAND2, NOR2, XOR2, INV, MUX2).
All documented state elements in design_brief.md must be described as posedge-triggered; exactly one instance in access_ctrl_netlist.v must actually be instantiated as DFF_NEGEDGE.
Instance and net names must follow plausible conventions consistent with the rest of the design (e.g. u_grant_ff, grant_pre) so the substitution is not detectable by naming alone.
The substituted negedge flop must sit on the path that samples the access-grant comparator output (grant_pre) before it feeds the final grant_out logic.
testbench_stub.v must provide a clock generator and stimulus sufficient to expose a half-cycle timing difference between posedge and negedge sampling of grant_pre via iverilog simulation.

functional_requirements.requirement: submission/trojan_report.json must be valid JSON containing the top-level fields trojan_detected (boolean), suspect_instances (array), and summary (string); missing or mistyped fields fail this check.

Each element of suspect_instances must contain non-empty string values for instance_name, cell_type, and sampled_signal that reference identifiers found verbatim in inputs/access_ctrl_netlist.v (evaluate.py cross-references the netlist text).
If trojan_detected is true, suspect_instances must contain at least one entry; if trojan_detected is false, suspect_instances must be an empty array (internal consistency check).
The summary field must be a non-empty string of at least 20 characters describing the finding.

interface: The netlist file inputs/access_ctrl_netlist.v defines module access_ctrl_top with ports: input clk, input rst_n, input [7:0] key_in, input req_valid, output grant_out. All sequential cells are instantiated from the cell_library.v primitives: DFF_POSEDGE (ports .clk, .d, .q, .rst_n) and DFF_NEGEDGE (ports .clk, .d, .q, .rst_n). The design_brief.md states the module's documented clocking discipline is single-clock, all state elements posedge-triggered on clk. Participants submit an answer file at submission/trojan_report.json (participants must NOT modify any file under inputs/). The JSON file must be a single object with exactly these top-level fields: "trojan_detected" (boolean), "suspect_instances" (array of objects, each with "instance_name" (string, exact instance identifier as it appears in access_ctrl_netlist.v), "cell_type" (string, exact primitive name such as "DFF_NEGEDGE"), "sampled_signal" (string, exact net name driving the .d port of that instance), and "justification" (string, free text)), and "summary" (string, free text overview of the finding). evaluate.py parses this exact schema; unparsable JSON or missing required fields fails the FR checks. evaluate.py may optionally invoke iverilog/vvp on testbench_stub.v against access_ctrl_netlist.v to cross-check that a reported instance's output value differs from a same-named posedge reference at the half-cycle sampling point, but the PASS/FAIL verdict is determined by grading the content of trojan_report.json against the hidden ground truth.
objective: You are given a synthesized gate-level Verilog netlist of an access-control module along with its design brief. Analyze the netlist's structural cell list and its clocking discipline to determine whether every state-holding element that participates in the documented single-clock design is instantiated with the same active clock edge as specified in the design brief, and report any instance that deviates from that discipline along with the signal it samples. Produce a JSON report identifying any anomalous flip-flop instance, the net it captures, and a short justification grounded in the netlist structure.
response_format: A single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json matching the schema described in public_spec.interface.
